question.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(1-t+{t}^{3})+{x}_{2}(1+t-{t}^{3})+{x}_{3}(2+t+{t}^{2}) & =-2t-2{t}^{2} \\ ({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3})+(-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3})t+{x}_{3}{t}^{2}+({x}_{1}-{x}_{2}){t}^{3} & =-2t-2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-2 \\ {x}_{3}=-2 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-1){R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-2 \\ {x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the  third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
2{x}_{2}+3(-2)=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=2.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}+(2)+2(-2)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ and therefore ${x}_{1}=2.$
